title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 99 (Punishment for default in meetings)

content.overview: If a company defaults in holding a meeting in accordance with section 96, 97 or 98, or in complying with a Tribunal direction under those provisions, the company and every officer in default are punishable with a fine up to ₹1,00,000 and, for continuing default, a further fine up to ₹5,000 for every day the default continues.
content.glance: If a company defaults in holding a meeting in accordance with section 96, 97 or 98, or in complying with a Tribunal direction under those provisions, the company and every officer in default are punishable with a fine up to ₹1,00,000 and, for continuing default, a further fine up to ₹5,000 for every day the default continues.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 99 (Punishment for default in complying with provisions of sections 96 to 98). If a default is made in holding a meeting in accordance with section 96, 97 or 98, or in complying with any direction of the Tribunal, the company and every officer of the company in default are punishable with a fine that may extend to ₹1,00,000 and, in the case of continuing default, a further fine that may extend to ₹5,000 for every day during which the default continues. The provision applies to the specified meeting/Tribunal-direction default; it does not replace the underlying duty to hold the meeting or comply with the direction. The topic remains under source and current-law review.

sections.heading: Trigger
sections.body: The section applies where a company defaults in holding a meeting in accordance with section 96, section 97 or section 98, or in complying with a Tribunal direction under those provisions.

sections.heading: Persons liable
sections.body: The company and every officer of the company who is in default are subject to the penalty stated in section 99.

sections.heading: Fine and continuing default
sections.body: The fine may extend to ₹1,00,000. In the case of continuing default, a further fine may extend to ₹5,000 for every day during which the default continues. The section text does not state a separate aggregate cap.

hypotheticals.question: Does paying a section 99 fine itself satisfy a Tribunal direction to hold a meeting?
